description: Tests cited as implementation evidence for requirements (decision 0010). Each citation names the requirement, the CI job that runs the test, the test file, the test's exact top-level name and what the test shows. The job fails when a test cited for it does not pass, and the evidence job publishes every citation's result for the run in the readiness report. A citation is partial evidence for its requirement: it never accepts the requirement, which needs the acceptance evidence and approvals the specification names.

citations.test: another workspace's identifiers are refused exactly like unknown ones and change nothing
citations.proves: Every private customer operation in the API contract that takes a workspace-owned identifier, called by another workspace with the owner's real identifier, gets exactly the reply an unknown identifier gets and changes none of the owner's rows.

citations.test: another workspace's identifiers are refused exactly like unknown ones and change nothing
citations.proves: On every private customer API operation that takes a workspace-owned identifier, in its path, body or query string, another workspace's identifier is refused exactly like an unknown one and changes nothing; every private listing shows another workspace none of the owner's records; client-chosen request keys are unique only within their workspace; and every table holding workspace rows is mapped to the cases that try its identifiers or to a recorded reason.

citations.test: every private operation with an identifier has a substitution case or a recorded reason
citations.proves: A private operation added to the API contract with an identifier and no substitution case, or no recorded reason for having none, fails CI.

citations.test: every identifier a private operation takes outside its path has a substitution case or a recorded reason
citations.proves: An identifier field added to a private operation's body, query string or headers, as the API's own request schemas declare them, fails CI until it has a substitution case, a client-key scope or a recorded reason.

citations.test: HTTP code cannot create, cast or redirect a workspace actor
citations.proves: No HTTP code can make, cast or redirect the workspace actor a service acts for; only the server's own resolution of a membership issues one.

citations.test: messages wait in the outbox and are offered to the sender once, after every check is made again (WRK-003, WRK-004, PAY-008, PAY-009)
citations.proves: Against PostgreSQL, in another workspace's database scope a message can be neither read, changed nor offered to a sender, in its own scope a message's recipient cannot be changed, and a row another workspace holds about the same record's id does not stand in for a workspace's own message.

citations.test: a workspace's log says what became of each message, never that one reached anyone, and the receipt downloads as a PDF (WRK-003, PAY-009)
citations.proves: Against PostgreSQL, another member of a workspace reads its delivery log and is told only that a message is not theirs, another workspace's log holds none of it, and a member who has left is refused.

citations.test: the email service's reports are recorded on the message or reminder they are about, whatever their order, and never on a message sent to no one (WRK-003)
citations.proves: Against PostgreSQL, another workspace's log shows nothing of a workspace's delivery reports; in that other workspace's database scope a report is neither read nor changed nor written for the first, and the reports as they arrive are no workspace's to read.

citations.test: row-level security limits customer requests to their own workspace
citations.proves: Queries with no workspace filter, run as a customer request through every database pool path, see only the request's own workspace rows.

citations.test: background work for one workspace reads it in that workspace's scope
citations.proves: Background work done for one workspace (document and workspace data exports, staff privacy exports, reminder delivery) reads that workspace's data in its database scope.

citations.test: missing, malformed, future and stale factor ages cannot establish MFA
citations.proves: A staff session whose second-factor age is missing, malformed, in the future or stale is not treated as multi-factor authenticated.

citations.test: production denies injected scripts, frames, objects and unconfigured origins while allowing required Clerk resources
citations.proves: The production content security policy allows scripts only by nonce, no inline or evaluated script, no objects or framing, no unconfigured origins, and fonts and styles only from the app's own origin.

citations.test: every change in the contract refuses a request from another site, counts it, and saves nothing
citations.proves: Against real PostgreSQL and the whole API, every change in the contract but the anonymous requirements check, sent as a page on another site could send it (from that site, with no origin or a null one, marked by the browser as from another or a sibling site, or with a body a form sends), is refused with 403 even for a member of staff who holds its role; each refusal is counted as denied access and no table changes, while the same kind of request from the site's own page is saved.

citations.test: markup saved through the API is drawn as text on the customer's and staff's screens, and none of it runs
citations.proves: Against real PostgreSQL, the real API and the real web app in a browser without the content security policy, hostile markup saved through the API in a business profile, a document, a template's answers, a task, a support request, a privacy request and a staff answer is shown on each customer and staff screen as the text typed, with no element it tried to make and no script it carried run, while the same markup put into a page as HTML on purpose runs and is caught.

citations.test: hostile text sent to every operation in the contract comes back only inside JSON with the security headers, fails no route, and stays text in the database and its searches
citations.proves: Against real PostgreSQL and the whole API, every operation in the contract, sent hostile markup and SQL text in its path, query and body, each query value twice and keys that would reach every object's prototype, answers in JSON or nothing, naming its character set, with nosniff, a policy that loads and runs nothing, no framing, a same-origin referrer policy and HSTS for a year, kept from shared caches when private and never with a failure of the server's own, and no request changes the prototype every object inherits; an unknown address, the API's folders, TRACE and a malformed or oversized body are answered the same way, the folders and TRACE with a JSON 404 that repeats nothing sent; every read, sent as each kind of caller, changes no table but the counts reads keep; SQL text comes back byte for byte, searches read %, _ and \ literally, and a NUL character is refused as a detail not taken.

citations.test: hostile markup in a page's address is drawn only as text: the server's HTML holds it escaped, and the page runs none of it (SEC-003)
citations.proves: On the compiled web app, the library, services, guides, industries and help pages given hostile markup in every value of their address hold it only escaped in the server's HTML, and in a browser run none of it and make none of its elements, while the search box of each page that has one shows it as text and the industries page says it back as text.

citations.test: product code puts no text into a page as HTML, and hands a browser HTML only where it is reviewed (SEC-003)
citations.proves: The raw-html repository rule fails on assigning innerHTML or outerHTML, insertAdjacentHTML, createContextualFragment, document.write, setContent and srcDoc in product code outside its two reviewed places, and the repository has none.

citations.test: product code builds no SQL from text but where it is reviewed, and each review counts its texts (SEC-003)
citations.proves: The raw-sql repository rule fails on sql.raw of anything but a fixed string and on a query whose text is a template with substitutions or a joined string, outside reviewed files whose count of such texts must match their review, and the repository has none.

citations.test: origin comparison includes scheme, port and exact serialized origin
citations.proves: The same-origin check compares a change's origin with the trusted site by scheme, host and port exactly.

citations.test: trusted site comes only from server configuration; production never falls back to a development hostname
citations.proves: The trusted site's origin comes only from the server's settings, and production never falls back to a development hostname.

citations.test: deep, broad and high-node-count JSON fails within fixed budgets
citations.proves: A body nested too deep, too broad or with too many values is refused within fixed budgets before any schema reads it.

citations.test: controlled acceptance preserves one bounded provider key and minimal stable body, not inbox delivery
citations.proves: A reminder email's body is the same whatever the task's title, and holds neither the title nor the account's identity, so no text a customer typed reaches the email.

citations.test: the linter CI runs refuses the code the security baseline counts on it to refuse
citations.proves: The linter CI runs on every merge refuses eval and code built from strings, raw HTML in JSX, script addresses in JSX, and comparisons that are not strict but against null.

citations.test: product code starts no shell: no exec or execSync from child_process, and no shell option (small hardening, part 4)
citations.proves: The repository rule no-shell refuses product code that takes exec or execSync from child_process, by import, require or a dynamic import, or writes a shell option where it starts a program, and finds none in the repository.

citations.test: the staff upload refuses a file over its limits before it reads it
citations.proves: The staff upload answers a file longer than 2 MB of base64 with 413, and one over 2 MB, empty or not plain base64, a Word package that expands past 12 MB or holds more than 300 parts, and a PDF of more than 100 pages, with 422.

citations.test: the staff upload refuses a file whose content is not its kind, or that carries a program
citations.proves: The staff upload refuses a PDF given as a Word file and a Word file given as a PDF, a package that is not a Word document, a Word package with a macro, an embedded object or a part named outside the package, and a PDF with a script.

citations.test: the staff upload refuses a Word file that declares a document type or an entity, or reaches outside itself
citations.proves: The staff upload refuses a Word file whose document or content types declare a document type or an entity, one with a picture fetched from outside it, and one with a reference outside Unicode.

citations.test: a standard Word file is read, and its text kept as written
citations.proves: A standard Word file's text is read as written, an entity it does not declare stays as written rather than being expanded, and a hyperlink out of it is kept as a link.

citations.test: an anonymous probe of a private object reports a redirect as its answer and never follows it (SEC-002)
citations.proves: Against a server of the test's own, the anonymous probe of a private object reports a redirect, or a refusal, as its answer and never asks for the redirect's target.

citations.test: only the anonymous probe addresses the storage service directly
citations.proves: No product source of the API but the anonymous probe addresses the storage service, so every probe of private storage refuses redirects.

citations.test: a sign-in token is accepted only when it was made for Valo's own site, and only as the provider signed it
citations.proves: Through the API's own identity middleware, with a synthetic instance's key and no call to the provider, a session token made for Valo's site signs its holder in, and one made for another site or for none, signed with another key or past its time, signs no one in.

citations.test: the repository has no silent catches, no import cycles and no unreviewed binding checks
citations.proves: The API has no import cycle, no unexplained empty catch, no unreviewed creation of a workspace actor or entry into a workspace scope, no unreviewed caller of the inference dispatcher's binding checks and no import past a module's public entry.

citations.test: code outside a module reaches it only through its index
citations.proves: The module boundary check reports code that imports a module's files other than its public entry, from outside the module or from another module.

citations.test: phase 2 migration chain preserves applied phase 1 SQL, staff access and history
citations.proves: Applying the later migrations to a synthetic database that already holds the applied phase 1 migrations keeps the applied SQL, staff access and history.

citations.test: R1 customer workspaces have no evidence upload and only the Content staff editor accepts a document
citations.proves: Customer request schemas accept no file bytes. Task inputs hold only structured fields. The staff editorial draft is the only JSON request carrying document bytes, and the web app exposes its file picker only on the staff screen.

citations.test: R1 calls Paystack only for one-time charges, refunds and disputes and keeps no subscriptions, wallets or payouts
citations.proves: Every Paystack call in the API goes through one function, to the transaction, refund and dispute endpoints only, and no database table holds subscriptions, plans, wallets, balances, splits, transfers, payouts or collections.

citations.test: checkout asks Paystack only for a one-time charge, with no plan, split, subaccount or saved card
citations.proves: Checkout initialisation sends Paystack exactly the fields of a single naira charge (reference, amount, currency, email, return URL and order metadata) and nothing that sets up a plan, split, subaccount or saved card.

citations.test: only one-time charge, refund and dispute events are processed; subscription, invoice and transfer events are not
citations.proves: The webhook processes only charge, refund and dispute events; subscription, invoice, transfer, payment request and dedicated account events are classed as not processed.

citations.test: the enquiry form asks for consent exactly when the API requires it
citations.proves: For every enquiry topic in the API contract, the web form asks for sharing consent exactly when the API refuses the enquiry without it: for every service topic, and not for product support.

citations.test: the enquiry form asks for sharing consent before a service enquiry and not for product support
citations.proves: The enquiry form does not send a service enquiry without explicit sharing consent and tells the person why; product support needs none.

citations.test: development PostgreSQL tenant, concurrency, history and durable-ticket proof
citations.proves: A service enquiry without consent is refused; with consent, its topic, scope, reply email and consent are saved, exactly one open support case is created for staff, and the receipt says “Enquiry received”, never that anything is booked.

citations.test: actual durable support intake, assignment, replies, triage, privacy and HTTP authority
citations.proves: A saved request opens exactly one support case with the same reference and full scope, which its own workspace can read and another workspace cannot.

citations.test: real PostgreSQL source correction, staff boundaries, abandoned jobs and final-dispatch ordering
citations.proves: Safety actions need an active staff role for their area and fresh MFA; a checkout pause stops new checkouts while AI still runs, free guidance reads the same with AI and checkout both paused, and the pause's reason, actor and customer impact are recorded in an append-only audit.

citations.test: source safety adds freshness, binding and sticky-hold checks without manufacturing eligibility
citations.proves: The source safety gate refuses a held item, a changed hash, a failed check and a stale review, so a hold takes the item out of use.

citations.test: actual durable support intake, assignment, replies, triage, privacy and HTTP authority
citations.proves: A hold placed by content staff from a support referral records one source impact and one audit row, and staff without the content role are refused.

citations.test: actual PostgreSQL saved-template ownership, durable state and blocked-release boundaries
citations.proves: A workspace owner's save is stored once and seen by every new read; other workspaces, non-owners and revoked members are refused; and a saved template that is no longer available keeps only its saved title, is reported as unavailable and can still be removed.

citations.test: recommendations use supplied activity/category and omit saved or absent releases
citations.proves: Recommendations follow the workspace's activity and category, leave out templates already saved and templates that are not released, and are empty when nothing is released.

citations.test: actual durable support intake, assignment, replies, triage, privacy and HTTP authority
citations.proves: Support and content work are kept apart by role: content staff cannot use the support queue and support staff cannot act on content referrals; a content hold from a referral records a review-work item and claims no AI review.

citations.test: actual dispute HTTP routers enforce managed finance authority, tenant binding and same-origin writes
citations.proves: Payment concerns and disputes are handled under the finance role: support staff, anonymous callers and stale, revoked or mismatched sessions are refused before anything is disclosed.

citations.test: actual HTTP privacy routes apply an independent privacy role and fresh MFA
citations.proves: Privacy requests are handled under their own privacy role with fresh MFA: a privacy-only identity can read and claim them and a finance-only identity cannot.

citations.test: real development access intake, privacy isolation and staff boundaries
citations.proves: Anyone can send a request to staff without signing in or paying; it is saved for staff and never dispatched anywhere else.

citations.test: original editorial60 corpus remains exact and all ten lifecycle cases keep their original preconditions
citations.proves: The 60 editorial cases stay byte for byte as authored, apart from the customer AI and rule corpora, and its ten lifecycle cases keep their deterministic preconditions.

citations.test: the score holds every case to EDP-010's bar and never accepts it
citations.proves: A run of the 60 editorial cases meets EDP-010's bar only when at least 57 pass and none is a critical false publication; blocked, unselected and unrun cases count as not passed, and the score never accepts the requirement or claims legal accuracy.

citations.test: the last retained run of the 60 cases is far from EDP-010's bar
citations.proves: Scored against that bar, the last retained run of the 60 editorial cases passes 14 with no critical false publication, so the bar is not met.

citations.test: builds the 14 case-bound cases whose texts are retained, and names what each of the other 17 needs
citations.proves: Of the 31 editorial cases bound to their own candidates, the 14 whose base candidate and cited passages the repository retains are built, and each of the other 17 names the text it still needs.

citations.test: each case changes its base exactly as the corpus's input mutation describes
citations.proves: Each built candidate is its retained base, read against pinned hashes, with only its case's input mutation applied; building one runs, scores and publishes nothing.

citations.test: EDP-010 C041: a review that fails at the provider is kept as a failure, never retried into a review or past the batch's limits
citations.proves: Case C041's review pair, run through the real dispatcher, ledger, binding checks and managed SDK transport against a local destination that refuses every request, is kept as two failure records with no invented answer; running it again sends nothing, the case stays blocked, other admitted work is refused before sending, and no safety switch is engaged.

citations.test: C060's reviews count only after C018's candidate was held by its real reviews in an earlier pair
citations.proves: The editorial suite counts case C060's reviews only after a pair for C018's current candidate, prepared before C060's own, has both reviews and at least one hold; otherwise C060 stays blocked, and its record names the pair that held C018.

citations.test: EDP-010 C060: the follow-up pair waits for C018's hold as the dispatcher records it
citations.proves: C060's pair is refused until C018's pair, run through the real dispatcher, ledger and managed SDK transport against a local destination that answers with synthetic holds, is recorded with both reviews holding; C060's fresh reviews of its own revised candidate then name that pair, with no provider call.

citations.test: the reviewer's record: an active reviewer's decisions, kept for good, from someone who prepares no content
citations.proves: Against real PostgreSQL, only an active reviewer with recent MFA reads the editorial corpus's 60 cases and records a decision on one, other staff learn nothing of the cases or the corpora, a decision says why in 20 to 2,000 characters and holds only for the case's hash as read, a later decision is added rather than written over, the database keeps every decision as written from an active reviewer only, and no one can hold the reviewer and content roles at once, an emergency content grant included.

citations.test: each case carries the hash the disabled allocation package binds it by, in the corpus's order
citations.proves: Each of the editorial corpus's 60 cases, and each case of the other two corpora, is read for the reviewer with the SHA-256 hash the disabled allocation package lists for it, in the corpus's order, so a decision names the hash a suite binds the case by; a case whose row changes gets another hash.

citations.test: phase 2 migration chain preserves applied phase 1 SQL, staff access and history
citations.proves: The acceptance reviews migration keeps every existing row and rolls back cleanly, adds the reviewer role, refuses the reviewer and content roles to one person whichever comes first, takes a decision only from an active reviewer with exactly the fields of its kind, dates it itself, and never changes, removes or truncates a decision. The acceptance runs migration keeps every existing row and rolls back cleanly, keeps a run only when each case names itself, its hash, its status, its review and the hash of the case as kept, once, dates a run itself and never changes, removes or truncates one, and takes a run decision only on a case a kept run left for a reviewer, with those hashes.

citations.test: an acceptance reviewer reads a corpus's cases with what a confirmation claims, and records a decision with why, bound to the case's words
citations.proves: On a phone with no automated WCAG 2.2 AA failure, the acceptance cases page shows what a confirmation claims, how many cases are confirmed, rejected and without a decision, and each case's expected outcome, critical failure conditions, sources and latest decision, and records a decision with why for the case's hash as read, holding the other cases and sets while one is started.

citations.test: a decision says who made it, when, and how many came before it
citations.proves: The acceptance cases page says on a Lagos clock who made a case's latest decision, when, and how many came before it, counts cases by their latest decision on their current words, and says that nothing on it accepts a case or a requirement.

citations.test: runs kept for a reviewer: every case as it stands, decisions bound to the case as kept, and nothing changed after
citations.proves: Against real PostgreSQL, with a kept run of the rule scenarios, the record that keeps each suite's run for a reviewer works as follows: a suite's command keeps a run only of every case of the corpus as it stands, in order; an active reviewer with recent MFA reads the latest kept run with the cases it left for a reviewer, and other staff cannot; a decision that the run met a case or did not says why and is refused for another run, another case or another hash of the case as kept; a later decision is added rather than written over, and a newer run is shown while the decisions stay with the run they were made on; and the database never changes, removes or truncates a kept run and takes a run decision only on a case a kept run left for a reviewer, as it was kept.

citations.test: the editorial suite leaves a held template with why and its two reviews, and a case-bound pair with its two reviews; a case with nothing kept leaves nothing to judge
citations.proves: A kept editorial run leaves each case the suite marks needs_evaluator_decision for a reviewer with what the run kept: a held template's version, why it was held and its two reviews, or a case-bound pair's two reviews and the case it follows; a case with nothing kept to read, such as C041, is listed with its reason and left with nothing to judge.

citations.test: the latest kept run says who kept it and when, the suite's own results, and where each case left for a reviewer stands
citations.proves: The acceptance cases page's kept run says on a Lagos clock who kept it and when, the suite's own results by status, where the cases left for a reviewer stand, and who made each case's latest decision on the case as kept, when and how many came before it.

citations.test: a case counts only when its expected outcome is confirmed and the suite passed it or its run was recorded as met; a rejected one is out of the score
citations.proves: With synthetic cases and rows, a kept case counts only when the latest decision on its expected outcome, for its own hash, is a confirmation and either the suite passed it or the latest decision on the case as kept in that run is met; a rejected expected outcome takes the case out of the score, and a decision on another hash of the case or on another run is never read. The score accepts nothing.

citations.test: the score names the rows it used, by id and hash, and only those
citations.proves: A kept run's score names every row of the record it used, by id and by the hash of the row as read, and only those, with a hash of them all that changes when a used row changes and not when an unused one does.

citations.test: the bar: 95% of scored cases for the editorial and customer AI corpora, every scored scenario for the checker, with no critical failure
citations.proves: The editorial corpus's bar asks that at least 95% of the scored cases count, 57 of 60, and a case the suite marks a critical false publication fails the bar however many count.

citations.test: a kept run scored with the record: confirmed and met or passed counts, rejected is out, and the score names the rows it used
citations.proves: Against real PostgreSQL, a kept run scored with the decisions a reviewer recorded counts a confirmed scenario the run met or the suite passed, leaves out a rejected one, does not read a decision on other words of a case or on an earlier run, names the eight rows of the record it used with the hash of each as read, gives the page the same score, and exports the run, the score and those rows to a new file, never over an existing one.

citations.test: the kept run's score says how many cases count of how many, what the bar asks, what is out of it, and that it accepts no requirement
citations.proves: The kept run's score on the acceptance cases page says how many scored cases count of how many, how many must count, how many are out of the score and how many are critical failures, and that it accepts no requirement.

citations.test: real PostgreSQL source correction, staff boundaries, abandoned jobs and final-dispatch ordering
citations.proves: A changed source capture blocks the affected rule at once, then flags the affected tasks, cancels their pending reminders and sends correction notices only to affected workspaces, leaving past assessments unchanged.

citations.test: source safety adds freshness, binding and sticky-hold checks without manufacturing eligibility
citations.proves: Content is refused when it is held, its source changed or failed checking, its source check is more than a day old or its high-impact review is more than 30 days old.

citations.test: new source-linked tasks recheck current eligibility before any insert
citations.proves: New tasks and reminders for a withdrawn or expired rule are refused, and the assessment they came from is unchanged.

citations.test: development saved assessments, task isolation, concurrency and reminder outbox
citations.proves: A source withdrawal flags a historical task for review without changing what the customer completed.

citations.test: source-family implementation, publication, period and freshness gates fail closed
citations.proves: The checker leaves out a rule that is withdrawn or whose review has expired.

citations.test: a version is due for review when its review date passes, or 30 days after its source check (90 for general content)
citations.proves: The conditions the source monitor queues reviews by count a content version or rule release as due once its review date passes, or 30 days after its source check for high-impact content and 90 days for general content.

citations.test: a template or guidance entry the API stops listing is gone from the next page view: its list leaves it out, and its own page says it is not available and does not name it (EDP-011)
citations.proves: On the compiled web server with synthetic data, a template and a guidance entry the API stops listing are gone from the next library and resources views, and their own pages say they are not available and do not name them, in the server's HTML and after the browser reads them again; downloads and the checker are not checked here.

citations.test: the daily check holds what rests on a page when its words change, not when only its bytes do
citations.proves: On a real database the daily check holds what rests on a web page as soon as the words read from it change, and holds nothing when the page returns different bytes with the same words; a file is still compared by its bytes. The rows are synthetic and the transaction is rolled back.

citations.test: actual DOCX and Chromium PDF preserve the complete exact candidate and required notices
citations.proves: A template's DOCX and PDF exports keep its complete text together with the AI-review disclosure, scope, limitations and source-check date, checked against the text read back from both files.

citations.test: every draft guide prints as a guide in Word and PDF, and the files hold everything in it
citations.proves: Each of the thirty draft guides, printed as Word and PDF in a guide's own layout, holds its complete text together with the AI-review disclosure, what it covers, its limits and its source-check date, checked against the text read back from both files. The drafts are unreviewed and unpublished, and each sample says so on every page.

citations.test: a template's detail page shows its source-check and review dates, the AI-review disclosure, scope and limitations
citations.proves: The notices on a template's detail page show the exact disclosure text, the date the sources were checked, the next review date, the scope and the limitations, and the page fills them from each released template's own values.

citations.test: the web app never claims lawyer approval, professional verification or guaranteed compliance
citations.proves: No sentence in the web app's source claims lawyer approval, legal or professional verification or guaranteed compliance unless it denies the claim.

citations.test: on a phone, the home page's hero links to both journeys, and one tap on either opens it
citations.proves: On an emulated phone, the home page the compiled web server renders has “Create a document”, to sign-up carrying that choice, and “Check my requirements”, to /checker, as its first two links, the same size, one under the other with documents first, and one tap on either opens that page; the visitor is signed out, since the identity provider cannot load in the test.

citations.test: on a phone, the opened mobile menu and the bottom dock each link to both journeys, and one tap on any of them opens it
citations.proves: On an emulated phone, on the home page the compiled web server renders, with the header's own links hidden, one tap on Documents, “Check requirements” or “Create account” in the opened mobile menu opens /library, /checker or /sign-up, and the bottom bar stays on screen after scrolling, with “Create a document” opening sign-up, carrying that choice, and “Check requirements” opening /checker.

citations.test: every server-rendered page has the same five header links and marks its own section, the guidance tabs join their three pages, and the footer has eleven links in three groups
citations.proves: On the compiled web server, every server-rendered public page's header lists Documents, “Check requirements”, Guidance, Pricing and Help in that order, and the footer's Product group lists Documents, “Check requirements”, Guidance and Pricing.

citations.test: the home page offers both actions in its hero, beside its tasks and at its end, lists its eight everyday tasks, labels its examples as made up, shows the template count the server read and uses no price words
citations.proves: In the HTML the compiled web server sends, the home page offers “Create a document”, to sign-up carrying that choice, and “Check my requirements”, to /checker, together in its hero and again at its end, lists eight document tasks that each lead to sign-up carrying the task, and offers the requirements check once more beside them.

citations.test: the sitemap lists the public pages and released items only, never accounts, drafts or staff pages
citations.proves: The sitemap lists the fixed public pages and the released items the configured origin's discovery endpoint returns, with their review dates, and drops any workspace, staff, account or traversal path it is given.

citations.test: public pages get a title, description and canonical URL; private or unknown pages get neither
citations.proves: Public pages and released items get their own title, description and canonical URL; workspace, staff, account and unreleased pages get only an unavailable-or-private title, and every page stays out of search engines until launch.

citations.test: the web app shows no testimonials, customer counts, ratings or regulator endorsements
citations.proves: No sentence in the web app's source shows a testimonial, customer count, rating or regulator or government endorsement unless it denies one, and every page's footer says no regulator endorses Valo.

citations.test: controlled PostgreSQL commerce mechanics — NOT real Paystack execution or publication
citations.proves: A price's terms cannot be edited in place: a change of price closes the current row and adds a new one, and the price change log records both. citations.test: only the publisher names the publisher's database connection

citations.test: a content version or a prepared candidate is added only by a session that logged in as the drafting login

citations.test: only the drafting paths name drafting's database connection

citations.test: actual preparation and prepared-candidate readiness bind another form without authoring, review, approval or publication

citations.test: an AI review's attempt is recorded only by the review login, a drafting attempt only by the drafting login, and none is removed

citations.test: only the review's record names review's database connection

citations.test: actual operational caller recovers an artifact failure from settled receipts without new attempts or SDK calls

citations.test: dependency detector fails on a harmless high canary and strips raw descriptions

citations.test: a reviewed advisory names its owner and is reviewed again within 30 days, or it blocks the merge (SEC-007)

citations.test: a moderate or low advisory blocks the merge unless it is recorded with its owner and fixed within 30 or 90 days (SEC-007)
citations.proves: A moderate or low advisory the audit reports keeps the dependency summary blocked unless a record of it at its own severity names an owning role and a date to fix it by at most 30 days (moderate) or 90 days (low) after it was recorded and not yet passed; totals no record accounts for block too, and an informational advisory does not.

citations.test: the bill of materials lists every package the lockfile installs, from the registry, with its version and checksum (SEC-007)

citations.test: a package from anywhere but the registry, or without a checksum, stops the bill of materials

citations.test: every week the workflow runs the dependency, secret and static checks, and nothing else (SEC-007)

citations.test: static driver keeps an honest sanitized outcome: finding

citations.test: durable reminder delivery controls; controlled transport, not real email

citations.test: development saved assessments, task isolation, concurrency and reminder outbox
citations.proves: After reminders are scheduled, turning them off makes the next dispatch of a due reminder end as cancelled without calling the controlled sender, and every reminder of the workspace is cancelled.

citations.test: messages wait in the outbox and are offered to the sender once, after every check is made again (WRK-003, WRK-004, PAY-008, PAY-009)

citations.test: an address whose email service sent a message back for good, or marked one as spam, gets no more optional messages, and only its checksum is kept (WRK-003, WRK-004)
citations.proves: Against PostgreSQL, a stop on an address is applied to optional messages alone, and just before the send: a due reminder to a stopped address is cancelled without its transport being called, while the receipt owed to the same member, a necessary message, is still offered to its sender and taken. citations.test: a reminder to an address Valo has stopped sending to never reaches transport, and neither does one whose suppression cannot be checked

The transport is the test's own.

citations.test: an unsubscribe link turns its workspace's reminders off without sign-in, records the choice, and does nothing else (WRK-004, PRO-002)

Enforced before dispatch: the reminder that was due is then offered to a sender, which is handed nothing. The link stops reminders only, and only for its own workspace: the task is as it was, and another workspace's reminders stay on. A link that is not Valo's, was changed, was made for someone who is not the workspace's owner, or is for a workspace that is not there, whose owner's access is off or whose deletion is recorded is refused in the same words and changes nothing, and the page's address refuses a request from another site. citations.test: a reminder carries its unsubscribe link in its words and in the headers a mail program reads, the same on every attempt, and never goes without one

citations.test: a link changed anywhere is no link, and neither is anything that is not one

citations.test: the unsubscribe page stops nothing when it is opened, asks once when its button is pressed and says what was stopped; a link that does not work is said to in the server's words, and a link with no token offers no button

citations.test: development PostgreSQL tenant, concurrency, history and durable-ticket proof

citations.test: no file the browser is sent may hold a secret setting's value or a secret's shape (SEC-002, OPS-004)
citations.proves: The same check finds a key, or any secret setting's value, in a file the browser is sent, naming the setting or the key's shape and never the secret.

citations.test: each database login is rotated, revoked in an emergency and restored, and the work that needs it stops with its own code while the process carries on (SEC-002, OPS-004)
citations.proves: Each of the four database logins is rotated with its script, revoked in an emergency with its open sessions ended, and restored. Revoked, its work stops with the login's own code, each ended session is reported with its code and nothing is thrown, and the application's own connection goes on working.

citations.test: a day's notices owe a workspace one message, from 07:00 the next morning on a Lagos clock, naming what changed (EDP-011, WRK-004)
citations.proves: Against PostgreSQL, with synthetic notices and the stand-in sender, which sends nothing: a day's correction notices, changed requirements and withdrawn templates owe the workspace's owner one message from 07:00 the next morning on a Lagos clock and not before, however many runs there are, and a week back at most; a template replaced by a later edition owes none. The message names that day's changes alone, counts each saved item to review once, and is cancelled when no notice is left. A workspace whose deletion is recorded is owed nothing. No message reaches anyone, and no change made through the product is followed to its email here: the notices are the test's own.

citations.test: a day's notices owe a workspace one message, from 07:00 the next morning on a Lagos clock, naming what changed (EDP-011, WRK-004)
citations.proves: Against PostgreSQL, a day's message counts and names its own workspace's notices alone; asked for from another workspace the day is not found, in that workspace's database scope it is not there to read, and no customer request can add, change or remove a day, its own workspace's included. The other workspace's log lists none of it.

citations.test: a day's notices owe a workspace one message, from 07:00 the next morning on a Lagos clock, naming what changed (EDP-011, WRK-004)
citations.proves: Against PostgreSQL, a workspace's data download lists the days whose notices owed it a message, by the id its message is about, and another workspace's lists none of them.

citations.test: a notices message names the day, each changed requirement and withdrawn template, and how many saved items to review, and links to the workspace page (EDP-011, WRK-004)
citations.proves: The notices message's words name the day, each changed requirement as replaced or withdrawn, each withdrawn template and how many saved items to review, link to the workspace page, and leave out a part with nothing in it.

citations.test: a notices message names the day, each changed requirement and withdrawn template, and how many saved items to review, and links to the workspace page (EDP-011, WRK-004)
citations.proves: The notices message says why it is sent, and that it is a necessary message about the account with no unsubscribe link.

citations.test: a day's notices are emailed from 07:00 the next morning on a Lagos clock, for a week back, naming ten of each sort (EDP-011)
citations.proves: Until 07:00 on a Lagos clock the day before is not yet owed its message, at midnight and at the turn of a year too.

citations.test: the messages screen says in plain words what has happened to each message and reminder, calls none of them sent, calls delivered only one the email service reported as delivered, and says of a message Valo only recorded that nothing was emailed
citations.proves: In a real browser with controlled answers, the Messages page heads a message about a day's changes with that day, says that the notices themselves are on the Workspace page, and links there and not to Purchases. The answers are the test's own.

citations.test: an enquiry nobody has taken, and one that has waited on Valo past its aim, raise their own alerts under the enquiries runbook, past their limits only
citations.proves: With synthetic readings, any enquiry nobody has taken and any enquiry waiting on Valo past 48 hours raise their own alerts, each named in plain words and owned by the enquiries runbook and the support role, and a reading that cannot be taken raises an alert of its own. It does not show a failed dispatch of a reply: no reply is sent by email yet.

citations.test: an enquiry nobody has taken, and one that has waited on Valo past its aim, raise their own alerts under the enquiries runbook, past their limits only
citations.proves: With synthetic readings, the two alerts on enquiries name the enquiries runbook and the support role as accountable, as a row of the operating runbooks does.

citations.test: request counts: each process's minutes add up, the readings take the last ten minutes, a week is kept, and reminders and jobs are read from their own tables
citations.proves: On a real database, with a synthetic enquiry: just received, it is counted as one nobody has taken; untouched for more than 48 hours it is also counted as waiting on Valo, and for a little less it is not; once someone has taken it, it is no longer counted as untaken; touched again, waiting on its customer or resolved, it is not counted as waiting on Valo.

citations.test: a new requirements check is offered where the server offers one: with the profile's save, on the home page and on the result it follows, and the result saved from it opens compared with that one
citations.proves: On an emulated phone, the business profile, the home page and a saved result, each showing the offer of a new requirements check, fit 360 and 320 pixels, move keyboard focus only to visible outlined controls clear of the bars that stay on screen, and have no automated WCAG 2.2 AA failure. This is an automated check, not a manual or assistive-technology review.

citations.test: PRO-003: a new requirements check is offered after the profile changes an answer the check reads, and the earlier result and the tasks are kept
citations.proves: The offer of a new requirements check is read from the workspace's own profile versions and saved results: another synthetic workspace's later result and its newer profile version, which holds the very answers this workspace changes to, alter neither the result the offer names nor the answers it lists, and that workspace is offered nothing.

citations.test: the message that confirms a save has a close button with a name, lies under the header and clear of the save button, passes the automated checks while it shows, and goes when the keyboard moves on
citations.proves: On an emulated phone and on a desktop, the message that confirms a saved business profile has a close button named for a screen reader that shows without a pointer over it, lies under the header and clear of the save button held at the foot of the screen, leaves the page beside it in reach, follows the header as the page scrolls, has no automated WCAG 2.2 AA failure while it shows, and goes once Tab has moved the focus from the save button to the control after it, where the focus then is; on the phone, no control the keyboard then reaches is hidden behind a bar that stays on screen. This is an automated check, not a manual or assistive-technology review.

citations.test: the message that confirms a save is reached with F8, and its close button closes it
citations.proves: On a desktop, F8 reaches the message that confirms a saved business profile, Tab moves to the message and then to its close button without dismissing it, and Enter on the button closes it.

citations.test: the keyboard moving on from the page's last control reaches the message that confirms a save, which stays while the keyboard is in it and goes once the keyboard leaves it
citations.proves: On an emulated phone, Tab from the page's last control moves the focus onto the message that confirms a saved business profile, which stays while the focus is on it and then on its close button, and goes once the next Tab takes the focus out of it. This is an automated check, not a manual or assistive-technology review.

citations.test: a page's search and filters make one address for each view, and the plain page keeps its plain address
citations.proves: The address made for a guides, industries or help view carries its search and its filter, leaves out an empty one so that the plain page keeps its plain address, drops the spaces around a search, and carries whatever a visitor types as text.

citations.test: an address gives back the search and the filter it was made with, and nothing longer than a search may be
citations.proves: Reading an address gives back the search and the filter it was made with, and from an address someone else wrote a search without the spaces around it and no longer than 120 characters, a filter no longer than 80, and the first of a filter given twice.

citations.test: the guides, industries and help pages keep their search and filter in the address: a copied address opens the same view, and Back undoes a change
citations.proves: On an emulated phone, a copied guides, industries or help address opens the view it names with the search box filled and the filter chosen; a changed filter and what is typed are in the address, the plain page keeps its plain address, an address written with spaces around its search is not rewritten, a space typed at the end of a search stays in the box, and the Back button undoes each change and refills the box.

citations.test: the server renders the view a guides, industries or help address asks for: the box holds the search, the filter is chosen, and the guides and industries listed are the ones found
citations.proves: On the compiled web server, the HTML for a guides address with a search and an industry lists the one guide found with the box filled and the industry chosen, the HTML for an industries search lists the industries it names, and the HTML for a help search fills the box and keeps every question.

citations.test: the library's filters, sort and page live in its address: the server renders the results an address asks for, a reload keeps them, a new search starts again from the first page, and clearing the filters empties the address
citations.proves: On the compiled web server, a library address with its category, access, industry, sort and page is rendered by the server as the results it asks for, survives a reload, and is emptied when the filters are cleared.

citations.test: the library's search box keeps a space typed at the end of a word while its address follows, so the next word can be typed, and Back refills the box
citations.proves: On an emulated phone, the library's search box keeps a space typed at the end of a word after its address has followed, takes the next word after it, is refilled by the Back button, and leaves an address written with spaces around its search as it is.

citations.test: the industries page waiting for its data shows a loading placeholder, then lists every industry and says of each that it has no guides when none is published; a search that names no industry says so and offers the whole list again
citations.proves: On an emulated phone, the compiled industries page shows a loading placeholder, no error and no industry while its data is held back, then every industry with "No guides yet" when none is published and the number of guides where some are, and a search that names no industry says so and offers the whole list again.

citations.test: the pricing page waiting to learn whether payments are on shows a placeholder, then says what the API answered; when the API refuses or cannot be reached it says they are switched off, and shows no error
citations.proves: On an emulated phone, the compiled pricing page shows a placeholder while it waits to learn whether payments are on, then says what the API answered, and says "Switched off" with no error when the API refuses or cannot be reached.

citations.test: the services, support, help, privacy and terms pages wait for nothing and have nothing that can fail to load: with the API failing each shows its whole content, and until the sign-in service answers each form's place shows the way to sign in or to write without an account
citations.proves: On an emulated phone with the API failing and the sign-in service unreachable, the compiled services, support, help, privacy and terms pages ask the API for nothing and show their heading and content with no placeholder, nothing waiting and no error, and the services and support pages show the way to sign in, to create an account or to write without one in their form's place.

citations.test: signed in, the support page says its list of requests is loading, says when there are none and offers another try when the list cannot be read; its form says what is missing, keeps what was typed when a save fails and says so, and saves on the next try
citations.proves: On an emulated phone, the support page of a signed-in customer says its list of requests is loading, says when there are none and offers another try when the list cannot be read; its form says what is missing and sends nothing, a save that fails says so and keeps what was typed, the button cannot be pressed while it saves, and the next try saves.

citations.test: the industries page waiting for its data shows a loading placeholder, then lists every industry and says of each that it has no guides when none is published; a search that names no industry says so and offers the whole list again
citations.proves: axe-core finds no WCAG 2.0, 2.1 or 2.2 A or AA rule failing on the compiled industries page at phone width with no guide published, or with a search that names no industry; no manual or assistive-technology review is recorded.

citations.test: the pricing page waiting to learn whether payments are on shows a placeholder, then says what the API answered; when the API refuses or cannot be reached it says they are switched off, and shows no error
citations.proves: axe-core finds no WCAG 2.0, 2.1 or 2.2 A or AA rule failing on the compiled pricing page at phone width once it says whether payments are on, or when the API refuses or cannot be reached; no manual or assistive-technology review is recorded.

citations.test: the services, support, help, privacy and terms pages wait for nothing and have nothing that can fail to load: with the API failing each shows its whole content, and until the sign-in service answers each form's place shows the way to sign in or to write without an account
citations.proves: axe-core finds no WCAG 2.0, 2.1 or 2.2 A or AA rule failing on the compiled services, support, help, privacy and terms pages at phone width with the API failing and the sign-in service unreachable; no manual or assistive-technology review is recorded.

citations.test: signed in, the support page says its list of requests is loading, says when there are none and offers another try when the list cannot be read; its form says what is missing, keeps what was typed when a save fails and says so, and saves on the next try
citations.proves: axe-core finds no WCAG 2.0, 2.1 or 2.2 A or AA rule failing on a signed-in customer's support page at phone width while its list is read, when the list cannot be read, with the form's missing details shown and after a save that failed, and the failed list and the failed save are each announced in a role="alert" element; no manual or assistive-technology review is recorded.

citations.test: the request the provider is sent for a reminder is, to the byte, what it was before the reminders moved onto the shared sender
citations.proves: A reminder handed to the shared sender reaches the email provider as the same request as before, with the same idempotency key and the same body in the same order, so a reminder retried across that change is the first request again and is sent once.

citations.test: the development mailer sends whatever message it is handed: one with no headers or labels goes without them, and only an optional one is asked about its address
citations.proves: The reminders' development mailer, as a sender of the shared kind, sends a necessary message without asking whether Valo has stopped sending to its address, and asks for an optional one alone: stopped, it sends nothing and says so. A key, a subject or a header that is not one plain line never reaches its transport.

citations.test: a reminder goes through any sender of the shared kind, as an optional message under its own key, and a sender's answer that the address is stopped is the reminders' own refusal
citations.proves: A reminder is handed to a sender as an optional message with its unsubscribe link in its words and headers and no task title or identifier in them, the same on every attempt. A sender's answer that the address is stopped is never taken for a sent reminder, and without its link a reminder is handed to no sender.
